title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: One direction leads; you can keep it, take an alternate, or ask for a new hand.

options.label: Security-Printed Instrument
options.lineage: cheques, demand drafts and banknote security printing
options.thesis: The portfolio is printed like a bank instrument: every case study is a numbered, verifiable document.
materials: security-tint paper with fine guilloche line fields
options.viewport: Name engraved large on pale security paper beside a live guilloche rosette drawn from your real figures; case study 01 sits below as a serial-numbered instrument with its MICR line, one click from opening.
options.risk: If overdone it reads as a cheque costume; the instrument details must carry real data, not decoration.

raised.raise: Each case study moves through fixed stations in order (source, clean, model, report) and shows which station each step belongs to.
Every figure is set in tabular numerals in ruled columns at real density, never as decorative big-number tiles.
One ink is reserved for the single commit action, Open case study, and nothing else uses it.
Margins carry edge codes: the MICR line on each instrument encodes project number, year and tools.

options.label: Audited Annual Report
options.lineage: printed annual reports and notes to the accounts
options.thesis: The portfolio as an annual report: highlights first, then numbered notes that back every figure.
options.viewport: A 'Highlights of the year' spread with your real figures, each footnoted to the case study that proves it.
options.risk: Familiar: close to where many finance-themed portfolios land, and can drift into broadsheet hairlines.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white bar fields and monospace columns.
options.viewport: A barcode wall with your figures packed in the margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly: finance recruiters don't recognise it and the abstraction hides the work.
options.risk: Strobing black and white repeats the effects you wanted gone.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Work develops station by station under amber light.
options.viewport: A dashboard developing out of grey in a tray.
options.case: Fuses weakly: a nice raw-to-report metaphor, but nothing a finance recruiter identifies with.
options.risk: Amber-on-dark reads moody rather than trustworthy.

options.label: Hardware Bench
options.thesis: Keycaps and knobs with one orange action key.
options.viewport: A key grid where each key opens a project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: product-design language, not finance.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the action that matters.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.thesis: Projects as frames on a scratched film strip.
options.viewport: A film strip with each frame a project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: artistic damage undercuts a message about accuracy.
options.risk: Grunge reads careless for a data-quality candidate.

options.label: Industrial Quote Labels
options.thesis: Everything labelled in quoted caps with hazard stripes.
options.viewport: "CASE STUDY" in giant quoted caps over a hazard stripe.
options.case: Fuses poorly: fashion irony clashes with a finance audience.
options.kept: Every zone named by its literal name.

options.label: Theatre Poster
options.thesis: Clashing silkscreen colour and a border packed with dates.
options.viewport: A collaged poster with dates in the border.
options.case: Fuses poorly, and its ray-burst motif is not something to use here.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, light developer-style portfolio executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role at top left, then a grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like most other analyst portfolios by design.
